affiliation.user:
Extract author affiliations and assess academic institutional or industry research lab credibility from this academic paper's first page. We choose the first page because author affiliation is often found in the first page of the paper. It is either alongside the author names, or using what is called superscripted author–affiliation markers or superscript footnote-style markers for affiliations.

Paper metadata:
arxiv_id: {{arxiv_id}}
title: {{title}}
abstract/summary: {{summary}}
authors: {{authors}}
category: {{category}}

First page text:
{{first_page_text}}

TASK 1: Extract Affiliations
- Identify all unique institutions/organizations/labs
- Map each author to their institution(s) if possible
- Handle superscript numbers linking authors to institutions

TASK 2: Assess Credibility Score (out of 10)
Evaluate institutional reputation specifically for {{topic_focus}} research. This profile tracks memory, storage, and compute for Physical AI (robotics, humanoids, ADAS, autonomous vehicles), aerospace & defense, XR, and edge AI, so robotics ecosystem enablers and memory/semiconductor leaders are elevated. The following are reference examples; use your best judgement from training data.

HIGH Tier use scores 8-10 (expect cutting-edge research, significant resources):
- Robotics/Physical AI ecosystem enablers: NVIDIA, Google (including Google Research and Google DeepMind), ARM, Qualcomm
- Memory and semiconductor leaders: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix, Intel, AMD, Western Digital, Kioxia
- Major universities: US Ivy League universities, MIT, Stanford, CMU, UC Berkeley, ETH Zurich, KAIST, Tsinghua, Georgia Tech, UIUC
- Research from Onur Mutlu or his co-authors (SAFARI group and collaborators)
- Fraunhofer Institute
- Robotics, autonomous vehicle, ADAS, and robotaxi startups with credible funding or deployments (e.g., Figure, 1X, Boston Dynamics, Agility Robotics, Waymo, Wayve, Zoox, Nuro)

SPECIAL RULE: Papers from major memory vendors (Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia, Western Digital/SanDisk) should ALWAYS be treated as high credibility even if the topic is somewhat adjacent.

MEDIUM Tier use scores 4-7 (established institutions with research capability):
- Universities such as University of Michigan, Colorado State University, CU Boulder, UC Irvine, and other known universities with CS/EE/robotics programs
- Tech companies with R&D divisions
- Government research labs (Sandia, Lawrence Livermore, NASA JPL, etc.)
- Established startups in memory, storage, robotics, or automotive compute

LOW Tier use scores 1-3 (limited track record or unknown):
- Unknown or obscure institutions
- No clear institutional affiliation
- Individual researchers without institutional backing
- New/unproven research groups

Your task is to evaluate this paper's significance for a team tracking advances in memory, storage, compute architectures, and AI algorithms that could influence next-generation Physical AI and XR systems, with emphasis on DRAM, HBM, LPDDR, PIM, NAND/SSD technologies, robotics, autonomous vehicles, aerospace and defense, functional safety, cybersecurity, and emerging AI models. Monitor how new workloads, system architectures, benchmarks, and standards drive future memory and storage requirements, performance, power efficiency, reliability, and product opportunities.

SCOPE GUIDANCE:
- IN SCOPE (memory/storage technologies): DRAM, HBM, LPDDR, DDR, 3D Memory, Processing-in-Memory (PIM), MRAM and emerging memory, memory architecture and packaging, memory pooling and CXL, NAND flash, SSD and NVMe storage, storage controllers, computational storage.
- IN SCOPE (Physical AI domains): DRAM memory and flash storage in humanoid robotics, robotics systems, automotive compute systems and safety, connected and automated vehicles, and aerospace and defense; other edge and embedded applications that require advancements in memory and storage.
- IN SCOPE (AI models and algorithms): new AI models/framework research for Physical AI topics such as humanoid robotics and ADAS, embodied AI and world models, especially from robotics ecosystem enablers like NVIDIA, Google, academic research, and robotics/ADAS/robotaxi startups; computing and algorithmic advancements (including AI) that enable Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and eXtended Reality (XR).
- IN SCOPE (safety, security, standards): safety (RAS, FuSa) and security from a memory, storage, and compute perspective, including standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508, ISO 21434, IEC TR 62380, and related functional-safety standards; humanoid robotics standards and benchmarks; automotive safety and standards.
- OUT OF SCOPE: energy storage, EV batteries, or power storage — these are unrelated to semiconductor storage. Score them low. Also score low papers where memory or storage is only briefly mentioned as context rather than a substantive topic, unless the paper qualifies through the Physical AI, XR, or safety/security scope above.

Field guidance:
- primary_topic: Identify the main technology or concept discussed. Choose the most relevant category from the list below, or use a specific variant (e.g., "LPDDR5X for Automotive" or "Humanoid VLA Model").

Primary Topic Categories:
- DRAM
- HBM
- LPDDR
- DDR
- 3D Memory
- Processing-in-Memory (PIM)
- MRAM and Emerging Memory
- Memory Architecture and Packaging
- Memory Pooling and CXL
- NAND Flash
- SSD and NVMe Storage
- Storage Controllers
- Computational Storage
- AI Accelerators and Compute Architecture
- Robotics and Physical AI
- Humanoid Robotics
- Autonomous Vehicles and ADAS
- Aerospace and Defense Systems
- AR/VR/XR Computing
- Edge AI Systems
- AI Models and Foundation Models
- Embodied AI and World Models
- Functional Safety (FuSa)
- Cybersecurity and Hardware Security
- Reliability, Availability, and Safety (RAS)
- Robotics Standards and Benchmarks
- Automotive Safety and Standards
- System Performance, Power, and Efficiency
- Emerging Semiconductor Technologies

- secondary_topics: List 2-4 related categories or concepts from the above list, or specify related technologies and application areas as an array.
- potential_impact: Use one of Low, Medium, High, or Breakthrough, followed by a concise explanation. A paper is highly impactful if it has: real hardware validation, major bandwidth or latency improvements, or findings likely to influence product roadmaps; reduces product costs; requires considerable change to current compute architectures (alternative compute architectures and products); represents a breakthrough in Physical AI algorithms; or is a key enabler for aerospace and defense (e.g., AI servers in space).
- relevance_score: 1-10. A paper should receive a high relevance score if it provides actionable insights into memory, storage, compute, or AI architectures that could influence future products, system design, or technology roadmaps for Physical AI, XR, automotive, aerospace, and edge AI systems. High-scoring papers should demonstrate one or more of the following:
  - Novel DRAM, HBM, LPDDR, NAND, SSD, PIM, CXL, memory pooling, or storage architectures.
  - Quantified improvements in performance, bandwidth, latency, power efficiency, capacity scaling, reliability, safety, or security.
  - New AI models, frameworks, or workloads that significantly impact memory or storage requirements.
  - System-level innovations for robotics, humanoids, ADAS, autonomous vehicles, XR/AR/VR, aerospace, defense, or edge AI.
  - Advances in functional safety, RAS, cybersecurity, or standards relevant to memory, storage, and compute systems.
  - Industry-impacting research from leading ecosystem contributors (e.g., NVIDIA, Google, major universities, robotics and autonomous vehicle startups).
  - Benchmarks, deployment studies, or real-world evaluations demonstrating practical applicability and scalability.
  - Emerging technologies with a credible path to commercial adoption or influence on future semiconductor and system architectures.
- Consider the memory- and storage-system implications of algorithmic and AI-model proposals (effects on memory capacity, bandwidth, data movement, power, or storage footprint) when assigning relevance.
- Lack of explicit hardware experiments should reduce confidence but not automatically disqualify a paper if memory, storage, or Physical AI system implications are clearly described.
- key_findings: Summarize the main technical contribution in 2-3 sentences.
- actionable: Indicate Yes, No, or Maybe, with one-sentence rationale.

Be technical but concise. Focus on practical implications for memory and storage requirements of Physical AI, XR, automotive, aerospace, and edge AI systems.

analysis.user:
You are analyzing a research paper with full-text access.

Paper details:
- ArXiv ID: {{arxiv_id}}
- Title: {{title}}
- Authors: {{authors}}
- Primary Topic: {{primary_topic}}
- Selection Reasoning: {{selection_reasoning}}
- Full Text: {{full_text}}

Provide:
1. A LARGE SUMMARY (300-500 words)
2. A SHORT SUMMARY (50-80 words)

## LARGE SUMMARY INSTRUCTIONS

Write as a research academic reading the paper thoroughly. Your summary must include:

**Problem Definition & Motivation**: What problem does this paper address? Why is it important? What are the limitations of existing approaches?

**Solution & Contributions**: What is the novel solution or contribution? What makes this approach different from prior work? Quote key phrases from the paper that capture the essence of the contribution.

**Methodology**: Describe the technical approach in detail. What architecture, algorithm, or technique is used? How does it work at a high level? Reference specific figures when discussing technical details (e.g., "As shown in Figure 3...").

**Experimental Setup**: What workloads, benchmarks, robots, vehicles, or datasets were used? What hardware (memory devices, SSDs, SoCs, GPUs, embedded platforms) or simulation setup? What metrics were measured?

**Evaluation & Results**: What were the key quantitative results? Quote specific numbers and comparisons. What do the results demonstrate?

**Critical Analysis**: State assumptions made by the authors. Note limitations or potential concerns. What questions remain unanswered? Are there areas where the claims might not hold?

**Implications for Embedded Memory, Storage, and Physical AI Systems**: How does this work impact memory and storage requirements, compute architecture, or system design for Physical AI, XR, automotive, aerospace, or edge AI systems? Emphasize product impact, deployment tradeoffs, architecture decisions, manufacturing implications, or competitive positioning. Only reference specific technologies (DRAM, HBM, LPDDR, PIM, NAND/SSD, CXL, specific AI models, safety standards, etc.) if the paper itself discusses or evaluates them. Do not speculate about technologies not addressed by the authors.

IMPORTANT FORMATTING RULES:
- Use descriptive paragraphs, NOT bullet points
- Quote liberally from the paper using quotation marks
- Reference figures explicitly ("Figure 2 shows...")
- Reason first, then conclude (think through implications before stating them)
- Be thorough and specific with technical details
- NEVER use LaTeX, MathJax, or dollar-sign math notation ($...$, $$...$$). Write all equations, formulas, and mathematical expressions in plain text (e.g., "E = mc^2", "O(n log n)", "2x + 3"). Use words where possible (e.g., "alpha", "sum of", "approximately").
- Length: 300-500 words per paper

## SHORT SUMMARY INSTRUCTIONS

Write a concise 50-80 word summary (2-3 sentences) suitable for direct insertion into a professional email. Should capture:
- The core technical contribution
- Why it matters for memory, storage, or Physical AI/XR/edge systems
- Key quantitative result if applicable
- Do NOT reference technologies unless the paper explicitly discusses them

Tone: Professional, technical, direct.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Output format (pure JSON, no code fences):
{
  "arxiv_id": "{{arxiv_id}}",
  "large_summary": "...",
  "short_summary": "...",
  "pdf_analysis_performed": {{pdf_analysis_performed}}
}


IMPORTANT: Note that the `arxiv_id` in your output should be a full link. For example: `"arxiv_id": "http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00862v2",`

If a paper's full_text is empty or pdf_success is false, set pdf_analysis_performed to false and provide analysis based only on the abstract.
